headings: The impacts of atmospheric aerosol particles represent the largest uncertainty in scientific understanding of the Earth's climate and the air we breathe. Our group studies the chemistry of these particles as we look to learn more about their impacts on the planet's energy budget via the formation of clouds and human health.

Our group studies the chemistry of these particles as we look to learn more about their impacts on the planet's energy budget via the formation of clouds and human health. Prather Group News Featured on UC San Diego's Impact: " Cleaner Air. Safer Communities ." Read our newest perspective on Understanding Aerosol-Mediated Disease Transmission in ACS Central Science. Read our publication on H2S levels in South Bay San Diego published in Science Read our new est publications on VOC Emissions Impact on Spatial and Diurnal Air Quality in South Bay San Diego, and their Persistence through Ocean Transport and Air-Sea Exchange . Read our newest publication on UC San Diego's SOARS facility and temperature impact on Sea Spray Aerosol Production . Read our newest publication on a robust low-cost portable method for unified size distribution measurements using Spider-MAGIC and OPS . Get to know The Airborne Institute's website. Prof. Prather received the prestigious National Academy of Sciences Award in Chemical Sciences , and AAAR The Susanne V. Hering Award . In the early part of her career, Prof. Prather and her research group developed a unique method, aerosol time-of-flight mass spectrometry (ATOFMS), for the on-line characterization of the size and chemical composition of atmospheric aerosols. Using ATOFMS and a wide array of other gas and particle instruments, the Prather group is now performing studies worldwide to better understand the role of aerosols in climate change.
